name: Interpol
label: Matador
lede: Daniel Kessler found his bassist in an NYU philosophy class and his drummer in a vintage clothing shop, and Interpol went on to make Pitchfork's record of 2002. It left Matador for Capitol, came back, and in 2024 played to an estimated 160,000 in Mexico City.

eras.title: A band with no name
eras.text: Daniel Kessler had been looking to put a band together for a while and pulled one from NYU and the East Village. Interpol drew decent crowds for three years, put out an EP in Scotland, and swapped drummers before any American label came calling.

years.big: "We don't have a name so no one knows who to go see again."
years.h: Daniel Kessler meets Carlos Dengler in an NYU philosophy class
years.p: Kessler, on why the band needed one. He had been after a band for a while: Dengler came from that class, [[Paul Banks|71db5060-324e-4cc5-8ca6-0070220ae000]] from the East Village, and Greg Drudy took the drums.
years.xp:
Kessler approached Dengler after class, drawn by his look. Dengler was headed for academia and bass wasn't his main instrument, but he said yes.

Las Armas and The French Letters were both considered before Interpol stuck.

years.h: Sam Fogarino trades a vintage clothing shop for the drum stool
years.p: He had been thinking of quitting music. Greg Drudy left for [[Hot Cross|7210704b-06de-42ee-beb6-44e65357b12e]] and [[Saetia|cd4f7c44-9ff3-4660-9f93-170fef83edfd]] and went on to run the label Level Plane.

years.h: Interpol's first release comes out in Glasgow, not New York
years.p: The band appears on Fukd ID No. 3, an EP in Chemikal Underground's series, two years before an American label signs it.

eras.title: Bright lights, dark suits
eras.text: Recorded in Connecticut with Peter Katis and released on Matador Records, Turn On the Bright Lights made Interpol the band everyone compared to Joy Division, and the band everyone else got compared to.

years.h: Interpol tracks its debut in Bridgeport, Connecticut
years.p: Producer Peter Katis records Turn On the Bright Lights at Tarquin Studios. The songs predate September 11, but the attacks changed how the band heard them.

years.h: Matador signs Interpol
years.p: The label is part of the independent Beggars Group. A June EP, Interpol, carries re-recorded versions of PDA and NYC.

years.src: Wikipedia: Turn On the Bright Lights · Wikipedia: Interpol (band)
years.h: Pitchfork puts Turn On the Bright Lights at No. 1 for 2002
years.p: Out August 19 in the UK and a day later in the US, it spends 73 weeks on Billboard's independent chart and goes gold in both countries.
years.xp:
By Wikipedia's certification figures it reached about 522,000 in the US and roughly a million worldwide. NME ranked it No. 10 on its year-end list, and by 2004 it had sold 300,000 copies.

The Killers, Editors and the xx have all been named as bands it shaped.

years.h: Robert Christgau files it under Dud of the Month
years.p: The record Pitchfork crowned best of 2002 gets Christgau's Dud of the Month in the Village Voice.

eras.title: The cult of Carlos D
eras.text: Antics brought UK Top 40 hits, support slots with U2 and The Cure, and eighteen months on the road. It also made the bassist a Lower East Side style icon, and wore the band out.

years.h: Antics sells 350,000 copies in four months
years.p: Back at Tarquin Studios for the follow-up, Interpol lands Slow Hands, Evil and C'mere in the UK Top 40, and the album goes gold in the UK and US.
years.xp: On the UK chart Slow Hands peaked at No. 36, Evil at No. 18 and C'mere at No. 19.

years.h: URB's cover line reads Interpol + The Cult of Carlos D
years.p: Carlos Dengler's leather and styled look make him the face of the band. By 2007 he drops the look and says it felt good to be unrecognized.

years.cap: Interpol at the 9:30 Club, Washington, March 25, 2005
years.h: Interpol opens for U2 and The Cure, then tells Radio 1 it's wiped out
years.p: Eighteen months into the Antics tour, the band admits to Zane Lowe at a Sunderland show how exhausted it is. Direction turns up on a Six Feet Under soundtrack.

years.h: Capitol Records signs Interpol away from Matador
years.p: Reports of the deal surface on August 14, and Matador confirms them on September 1.

eras.title: Major label, minor misery
eras.text: The Capitol album was Interpol's biggest chart hit and, in Banks's words, its worst experience. Then Dengler quit, the band went back to Matador, and a borrowed bassist from Slint passed through.

years.cap: Paul Banks and band at Super Bock Super Rock, Lisbon, July 2007
q: the worst experience the band ever had working on an album
years.h: Interpol's biggest chart run comes with its worst studio experience
years.p: Our Love to Admire, the first album made in New York, with Rich Costey at Electric Lady and the Magic Shop, peaks at No. 4 in the US and No. 2 in the UK.
years.xp: Banks told Vice that major-label pressure was to blame. Keyboards were in from the start for the first time, and Kessler called them a fifth member. Interpol headlined Lollapalooza in Chicago that August.

years.h: Julian Plenti turns out to be Paul Banks
years.p: Banks releases Julian Plenti is... Skyscraper under the alias, with Peter Katis mixing at Tarquin.

years.h: Carlos Dengler is out, announced on the band's website
years.p: Sam Fogarino later says Dengler was tired of touring and of bass, never his preferred instrument. David Pajo of [[Slint|2869c510-2679-4a3f-bf15-e5e8b49f2f28]] covers on tour.
years.xp: Dengler later earned an MFA in drama from NYU's Tisch School and staged an autobiographical one-man show, Homo Sapiens Interruptus, at the 2016 New York Fringe.

years.h: Interpol goes home to Matador for its self-titled fourth album
years.p: Management changes at Capitol free the band. It is Dengler's last record.

years.h: Brad Truax takes the bass when David Pajo steps back
years.p: Pajo leaves to spend time with his family. That July Interpol opens for U2 at Chicago's Soldier Field.

years.h: Reading and Leeds close the run, then Interpol takes a break
years.p: Sam Fogarino says the band needs a big break. The members scatter into side projects, among them Paul Banks's second solo album.

eras.title: Banks picks up the bass
eras.text: Down to a trio, Interpol stopped looking for Dengler's replacement in the studio: Banks played bass himself. Meanwhile the ten-year-old debut turned into a victory lap.

years.h: Ten years on, the debut gets demos, live cuts and two rarities
years.p: The anniversary remaster of Turn On the Bright Lights adds the hard-to-find Get the Girls and Cubed.

years.cap: Interpol on the El Pintor tour
yt: All the Rage Back Home, official video
years.h: El Pintor turns out to be an anagram of Interpol
years.p: Paul Banks came up with the title while sketching merchandise. He plays bass on the record, and Brandon Curtis of The Secret Machines plays keys.

years.h: A snowstorm parks Interpol's bus in Buffalo for 50 hours
years.p: The El Pintor tour sits in Buffalo, New York, for more than 50 hours. Two Canadian shows and one in Boston are postponed.

years.h: For the 15th anniversary, Interpol plays the debut straight through
years.p: The tour runs Turn On the Bright Lights from start to finish.

years.h: Interpol announces Marauder in Mexico City
years.p: The sixth album is unveiled at a June press conference there, with The Rover as the first single.

years.h: Streaming services lose Our Love to Admire
years.p: A licensing dispute pulls the Capitol album off streaming. Paul Banks tells fans on Twitter to hang tight.

eras.title: The biggest room they ever played
eras.text: Matador bought the whole catalog back, and Interpol grew into a stadium act in Latin America. In 2026 the touring bassist and keyboardist were finally made members.

years.h: Matador buys Interpol's entire back catalog
years.p: That includes Our Love to Admire, which ends the licensing mess.

years.h: The Other Side of Make-Believe starts online and finishes in London
years.p: Begun over the internet during the pandemic, then written in a Catskills house and recorded in London with Flood and Alan Moulder.

years.h: Chris Broome plays drums while Sam Fogarino has spinal surgery
years.p: Broome fills in as Fogarino recovers.

years.h: Interpol plays a free show for an estimated 160,000 in Mexico City
years.p: The Zócalo crowd is the largest of the band's career. Interpol then tours Antics in full for its 20th anniversary.
years.xp: Wikipedia calls it the largest show of Interpol's career, played in the city's main square.

years.big: "I retired from the bass. I passed the mantle."
years.h: Brandon Curtis and Brad Truax become official members
years.p: Banks, announcing This Mirror Weighs a Ton on Partisan Records, says Truax wrote and played the basslines. Urian Hackney, then [[The Walkmen|b7834ebd-64ae-46c3-a930-2d3a52ee743a]]'s Matt Barrick, drum on tour.

years.h: This Mirror Weighs a Ton is Interpol's eighth album
years.p: Its first on Partisan Records, with Sam Fogarino contributing and Curtis and Truax credited as members.
